newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to launch seat belt drive - report.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to launch seat belt drive - report.

text.p: The Clinton administration plans to launch a national campaign to encourage 85 percent of the nation's drivers and passengers to wear seat belts by the year 2000, the Washington Post reported Wednesday.
The newspaper said Transportation Secretary Rodney Slater would announce the program Wednesday.

The administration estimated that improving seat belt use to 85 percent would boost the number of lives saved in U.S. highway crashes to 13,723 annually and reduce crash-related medical costs by $6.7 billion a year, the Post said.
By 2005, the administration hoped to get 90 percent of the nation's vehicle occupants to use seat belts, the report added.
The initiative comes amid intense debate over the future of air bags, which have saved an estimated 1,823 lives since manufacturers began installing them in cars and trucks in large numbers in 1986.
But since 1993, air bag deployments also have killed 39 children and 24 adults, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.
The NHTSA's figures show that an estimated 68 percent of Americans currently use seat belts, saving 9,529 lives a year. Wednesday, 16 April 1997 03:25:58
